page.description: Clonezilla Live editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A live system for imaging and cloning disks: it boots from a stick, copies partitions or whole drives, and writes nothing until you tell it to. There is one official image.
pros: Images and restores whole disks or single partitions.
Runs from a live stick, so the machine it works on needs no install.
Reads and writes many filesystems, including NTFS and ext4.
Free, and the only image is a single amd64 ISO.
cons: A text menu interface, not a desktop; mistakes are easy to make.
Cloning or restoring overwrites the target disk without a safety net.
Only amd64 is published as a stable ISO.
The Commons screenshot shows an old menu, not 3.3.3-37.
page.previewNote: A stock screenshot of the Clonezilla boot menu from Wikimedia Commons. It is not 3.3.3-37 and not a ROMinit recording: no image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted for this page.

page.status: One path: the amd64 ISO, written with dd or any image writer. Writing erases the stick; the tool then writes only the disk or partition you select, and restoring replaces its contents.
